title: Named textbook theorems of logic are those not derivable from simpler ones

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Named textbook theorems of logic are those not derivable from simpler ones

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: If the theorems of basic logic are listed in order of increasing complexity, the ones that cannot be derived from simpler theorems earlier in the list are almost exactly the ones traditional textbooks single out and name as interesting.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And remarkably enough what I have found is that these theorems are almost exactly the ones highlighted on the previous page that have traditionally been identified as interesting.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Implications for Mathematics and Its Foundations” (from p. 772), p. 818. Scope: theorems of propositional logic and the named laws in logic textbooks

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-44: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing formal and textbook resources permit a reproducible comparison for a chosen corpus and ordering. They cannot establish the claim invariantly because both the complexity measure and historical textbook sample materially affect the result.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fix a syntax-based theorem complexity ordering, compute which tautologies are not derivable from earlier selected theorems under the intended basis criterion, and compare that set with named laws from a preregistered textbook corpus. Precision, recall, and null-ordering comparisons quantify the match.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The textbook sample and meaning of interesting may be selected after seeing results.

The result depends strongly on notation and complexity ordering.

Named laws are historically dependent.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Propositional entailment is decidable, so the filter that keeps theorems not implied by simpler ones is an ordinary computation, and the named laws are a small explicit list. Open textbooks supply those names. Corpus choice is a limited confound and can be fixed in advance, so the comparison can be run now and can confirm or refute the reported match.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Generate propositional tautologies in order of increasing expression size and mark those not entailed by the conjunction of earlier ones. Compare that set with the named Boolean laws in a fixed collection of logic textbooks. A close match confirms the claim; a large symmetric difference refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The second distributive law is derivable from earlier theorems and is still traditionally named, so almost exactly needs a stated tolerance.

A different corpus of textbooks could name a different subset.
